scope: Stage8 independent read-only design review: runtime construction/ownership separation at current Controller and UnityLogicalLoop boundaries
recommendation: Introduce a normal GameplayRuntimeSession owning input/providers/core references and the existing injected logical loop. Preserve Controller scheduling and per-frame ordering for this bounded step; do not add an Update or a second clock.

observedCode.controllerLogicalLoop: DungeonBattleController.cs:102 constructs readonly UnityLogicalLoop(observeEditor:true) before Start. Editor pause subscription begins at construction.
observedCode.loopDispose: UnityTimeProvider.cs:50-65 subscribes/unsubscribes Editor pause events; Dispose does not clear clock, input queues, pending commands or observation timestamp.
observedCode.pump: Controller LateUpdate captures timestamped input, pumps all due logical frames, applies pending floor and refreshes UI in existing order.
observedCode.replacement: ReplaceManager cancels transitions, detaches views/events, resets timeline, replaces manager, binds session, then reconfigures and activates restored state.
observedCode.retry: Startup rollback resets the same loop for retry, while final Stop disposes it.

boundedSteps: Construct the existing gameplay loop at the same lifecycle point, then transfer explicit disposal ownership to Runtime rather than lazily creating a new loop on Start. Keep legacy pre-Start alias usable.
Runtime creates Input/Random/Logger once per successful attempt via explicit inputs; Controller keeps serialized configuration/Core factory and view binding policy.

Runtime accepts a constructed DungeonBattleManager through a single replace method. Keep Controller event detach, async cancellation, timeline-reset boundary and new view binding in their current order.
GameSystem.Session owns Runtime once, while legacy non-managed startup uses the same Runtime with a local owner. Do not maintain two independent owners for the loop/input.
Use separate attempt rollback and terminal Dispose: failed startup can release newly-created input/Core without disposing the pre-Start loop needed for retry.
Keep dialogueLoop and explorationResumeLoop in their current presentation-control ownership initially; do not merge their distinct time domains into the gameplay loop.
pitfalls: Do not use Time.frameCount to skip a second logical step in one render frame. Pending catch-up frames, event timestamps, input generation, queued commands and remainders must survive unchanged.
Do not reset/recreate loop or RNG when a View is rebuilt or a Core manager is merely rebound.
Reflection field aliases may be assigned by tests, not only read. Inventory write sites; aliases must not silently diverge from the runtime source of truth.
Disposal must cancel input subscriptions and pending callbacks before View/host ownership disappears, with idempotent managed/local finalization.
Loop.Dispose alone is not a queue reset; use existing StartNewTimeline only at the existing rollback/replacement boundaries.
Runtime must not capture arbitrary UI factories/View delegates; otherwise extracting construction simply moves the giant Controller dependency graph.
verificationRequired: Pre-Start clock access and Editor pause subscription count
